title: Observability for Function Calling
query: Your function-calling agent is in production. Users report it 'sometimes doesn't work'. What's the MOST important metric to track first?

options.text: Average response latency across all queries
Function call success rate broken down by function name
Total number of tokens used per day
LLM model version and provider uptime

explanation: For debugging 'sometimes doesn't work', you need FUNCTION-LEVEL SUCCESS RATES. This reveals: (1) Which specific functions are failing, (2) Whether it's selection errors vs execution errors, (3) Patterns in failures. Latency (A) doesn't indicate correctness. Token usage (C) is cost, not reliability. Model uptime (D) would affect all queries, not 'sometimes'. Key insight: aggregate metrics hide failures. You need per-function breakdown: calls, successes, parameter validation failures, execution errors, and latency percentiles.
learning_points: Aggregate metrics hide important failures in production
Track success rate per function, not just overall
Distinguish: selection errors (wrong function) vs execution errors (right function, bad params)
Use structured logging: query, selected_function, parameters, result, error
Alert on: sudden drops in success rate for any function
Dashboard must show: per-function metrics, error types, example failures

function_level: Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) per function
query_level: No function selected when one was needed
Wrong function selected (if you can detect)
system_level: Cache hit rate (if using prompt caching)

debugging_workflow: 1. Check per-function success rates → identify failing functions
2. Sample failed calls for those functions → identify patterns
3. Check parameter validation errors → schema issues?
4. Check execution errors → function implementation issues?
5. Review queries that selected wrong function → prompt engineering issues?
6. Compare to golden dataset → regression detection
alerts_to_configure: Function success rate drops below 95% for any function
Token usage spikes (possible prompt injection or loop)
